Next 7 days (through Wednesday)...

We expect to see an active weather pattern over the next 48 hrs or
so. Modest ridge with westerly flow over our area today will see
falling heights as short wave energy tracks through the northern
Rockies and Montana tonight into Friday. Strong winds in the south
central MT foothills are expected ahead of and behind this system. 
There is a chance of scattered snow showers over the high country
tonight into Friday, with some areas of light rain over the
eastern plains as well. Another shortwave system will track 
across the region Friday night through midday Saturday. Despite 
fast moving, this system has better potential for mountain and 
foothills snow, possibly spreading a mix of rain and snow to 
nearby lower elevations as well. 

Currently, the pressure gradient over the Paradise Valley and
foothills was around 14 mb with 700 mb winds 35-45 kts. This has
produced gusts well into the 60s along the I-90 corridor near 
Livingston since last night. As the frontal passage tonight moves
through (after 2 AM) we may see a brief drop in wind speeds at 
Livingston/Nye while winds increase along the US-191 corridor from
Big Timber to Harlowton where gusts 50-60 mph are possible Friday. 
For the remainder of the foothills area, strong winds are 
expected to increase through Friday morning, decreasing into the 
evening. Motorists of high profile vehicles should use caution in 
these areas through Friday. 

Precipitation Outlook...Mountain snow is expected to begin tonight
as the first shortwave moves through. Some weak frontogenesis may
produce some light rain over the eastern plains, mainly Rosebud
County eastward later tonight through Friday morning.

As the next weather system moves into our region Friday evening 
ascent increases over our western zones. We should see any rain
change over the snow fairly quickly in the foothills based on
progged soundings. Snow levels start out a little over 6Kft and 
drop to near 4kft by Saturday morning. Winds switch to a more
northerly flow behind the associated front after 09Z which is a
decent upslope component for the Beartooth and Red Lodge 
foothills. The period from 09Z to 15Z may see the most efficient 
snow producing conditions along the northwest facing slopes of 
the mountains as well as the foothills. The chance of at least 2 
inches of snowfall ranges from 45% at Livingston to over 80% at 
Red Lodge. Another wrinkle we are monitoring is a flash freeze 
type scenario toward early Saturday morning where melting snow on
roads freeze as air temps drop quickly below 32 degrees (this is 
especially true near Livingston). With all this in mind we have 
issued Winter Weather Advisories for lower elevation/foothills of
Park County as well as the Beartooth and Red Lodge foothills from
8 PM Friday to noon Saturday. Accumulations of 1-3 inches may be 
common with 2-4 inches in the steeper terrain near Red Lodge. 
 
The Winter storm warning remains valid for the Absarokas/Beartooths
from midnight tonight until noon Saturday. As dynamic lift shifts
southeast we should see snow pick up over the Pryors and northern
Bighorns. We have issued Winter Weather Advisories for the 
Pryors/Bighorns from 5 PM Friday through 2 PM Saturday. The 
heaviest snow should be early Saturday with 4-8 inches possible. 

Other areas from Billings west and south may see pockets of rain
Friday evening turn to a mix of rain/snow overnight into early
Saturday, but little if any accumulations are currently expected,
even in grassy areas. Less chance of much precipitation further 
east over the plains with this second short wave. 

Highs through the weekend will range from mid 40s to lower 50s
Friday, cooling off to upper 30s to mid 40s for Saturday/Sunday. 
Look for brisk winds from the northwest out east Saturday as well
(25-35 mph). 

Ensembles suggest weak ridging or westerly flow to start the next
week with seasonable temps. There is a hint of a split trough 
moving through the region at midweek which may bring unsettled 
weather...but it does not look like much of any organized forcing 
at this time. This will be something to watch as it approaches. BT
